clue.text: Writing about border in bloom

indicators.note: about means going round, so the writing wraps around the border

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A piece of writing discusses the edge of a flowerbed in full flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower, so it is an example of a bloom.

clue.text: Plant in vessel with a short lid

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a top is a lid

explanation.surface: A plant is sitting in a pot whose lid is too small.
explanation.definitionFit: The potato is a plant grown for its edible tubers.

clue.text: Abuse popular American returning to Lithuania

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: US stands for United States, so American
LT is the international code for Lithuania

explanation.surface: A well-liked American going back to Lithuania meets mistreatment.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult is a rude, scornful remark, a form of verbal abuse.

clue.text: Regretting exercising authority without latitude

indicators.note: without means the letter for latitude is removed

parts.note: ruling means governing or exercising authority

explanation.surface: A ruler regrets using power without any freedom to act.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to be sorry for it, so ruing is feeling regret.

clue.text: Recover silver in cream

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the silver goes into the cream

parts.note: a salve is a soothing ointment or cream
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A recipe to restore tarnished silver by soaking it in cream.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage is to rescue goods from loss, as from a wreck, so to recover them.

clue.text: Agricultural tool with hard shaft

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an arrow is a shaft fired from a bow

explanation.surface: A farming implement is described as having a tough handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrow is a frame of spikes or discs dragged over ploughed land to break up the soil.

clue.text: A simpleton raised head in distance

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, and in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a fool is a simpleton
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A fool lifts his head and stares into the far distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloofness is emotional distance, keeping oneself apart from others.

clue.text: Grass diet unexpectedly revised again

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grass-only diet has been reworked once more without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit a text is to edit it a second time, so to revise it again.

clue.text: Seeing wife infectious but not with cold

indicators.note: not with means the letter for cold is removed from the word

parts.note: catching means infectious, of a disease
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Seeing that a wife is contagious, though not with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' looks like the illness that makes the wife infectious, but it is only the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching means looking at or observing, the same as seeing.

clue.text: Ball in cricket match — one caught by short leg

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: A cricket report: during a Test, one batter is caught by the fielder at short leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Short leg is a real fielding position close to the batter, which hides that 'short' is clipping LEG to LE. 'Ball' looks like the cricket ball but is the anatomical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball is a common slang word for a testis, the male reproductive gland.

clue.text: Warning by way into woods

parts.note: fore is the warning shouted by golfers to people in the path of the ball
St is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way

explanation.surface: A warning sign posted beside a path leading into the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area covered with trees, which is what woods are.

clue.text: Bird jaw

definitions.meaning: a small songbird, such as the stonechat
to jaw is informal for to talk at length

explanation.surface: A bird's jawbone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a family of small songbirds and an informal talk or natter.

clue.text: Great help unravelling wire

indicators.note: unravelling means coming apart and being rewound differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Untangling a coil of wire turns out to be a great help.
explanation.definitionFit: Wire is an old word for a telegram, and by extension the telegraph that sends it.

clue.text: Note about sex and religion

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the note is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: fah is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
it is a coy old word for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A memo concerning sex and religion, two topics best avoided at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A faith is a system of religious belief, such as Islam or Christianity.

clue.text: European vote announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for vote is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: The result of a European vote has been announced.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pole is a native of Poland, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Gold trunk artist gives musicians

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a chest is a large box or trunk, and also the trunk of the body
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist hands a trunk of gold over to some musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of instrumental musicians playing together.

clue.text: Article with strap in it

parts.note: the is the definite article
a rein is a strap used to guide a horse

explanation.surface: A newspaper article comes with a strap tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal adverb meaning in that place or thing, the same sense as the phrase.

clue.text: Marksmen nose inside ship

indicators.note: inside means the nose word goes within the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
hooter is British slang for a nose

explanation.surface: Snipers poke their noses out from inside a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooters are people who shoot, so riflemen or marksmen.

clue.text: Swooping around Northern Ireland looking for water

indicators.note: around means the swooping word goes round the region's letters

parts.note: diving means swooping down steeply

explanation.surface: A bird swooping over Northern Ireland in search of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Divining, or dowsing, is searching for underground water with a rod.

clue.text: Hot look wounded Bob perhaps

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an air is a look or manner
cut means wounded by a blade

explanation.surface: A man called Bob looks hot and has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob reads as a man's name; here it is the short hairstyle, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short hairstyle cut level around the head, one kind of trim.

clue.text: Lean on inverted instrument

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, and in a down clue the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to abut is to border on or lean against

explanation.surface: Someone props themselves on an upturned musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is a large low-pitched brass instrument.

clue.text: Causes a commotion about boxing lawsuit

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the found letters are read backwards
boxing means enclosing, so the letters sit inside the phrase that holds them

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a fuss over a court action involving boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' marks ESAC sitting inside 'causES A Commotion', and 'about' turns it round. The surface makes boxing sound like the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is a suit brought before a court of law.

clue.text: Palace attendant having no time for messenger

indicators.note: having no means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a courtier is an attendant at a royal court or palace

explanation.surface: A royal attendant is too busy to act as a messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is someone who carries messages or parcels, a messenger.

clue.text: Tradesperson is more obscene we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is listened to, so its spoken form gives the letters

parts.note: grosser means more coarse or obscene

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a shopkeeper is even filthier than before.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food and household goods, a trader.

clue.text: Carnivore hunting yak and elk notices antelope first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of every word in the run

explanation.surface: A predator on the hunt spots yak, elk and finally an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' sits at the end but takes the initials of all six words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyaena is a meat-eating African mammal, a carnivore that hunts and scavenges.

clue.text: Express an opinion about love and desire

parts.note: love means nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O
to pine is to long or yearn for something

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth on the subject of love and longing.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state a view, a formal verb for voicing what you think.

clue.text: Confused about shrub initially lacking fruit

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the confused word wraps round the trimmed shrub

parts.note: blurry means indistinct or confused

indicators.note: initially lacking means losing the first letter

parts.note: hebe is an evergreen shrub from New Zealand

explanation.surface: A muddled gardener talks about a bush that has no fruit on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hebe is a New Zealand shrub that many solvers won't know; 'Confused' looks like it signals an anagram, but here it is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueberry is a small dark-blue edible berry, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Man to live with Nancy off and on

parts.note: to be means to exist, to live

indicators.note: off and on means taking every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A man who lives with Nancy only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Benny is a man's first name, a pet form of Benjamin or Benedict.

clue.text: Turfs out unruly civets

indicators.note: unruly means out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A householder throws out some badly behaved civet cats.
explanation.definitionFit: To turf out is an informal phrase for to expel someone from a place.

clue.text: Flying pelican holding tail of salmon in crest

indicators.note: holding means the shuffled bird keeps another letter inside it
flying suggests letters moving about, so these letters are rearranged
tail of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pelican in flight carries a fish's tail up to a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a high peak or summit, like the crest of a hill.

clue.text: Token is returned by gutted Glaswegian gangster

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the short word is read backwards
gutted means emptied of its insides, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A token comes back from a Glasgow hoodlum who is very disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' reads as British slang for upset, but here it hollows out Glaswegian to G and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal can be a sign or indication, as a token of something is.

clue.text: Old neighbourhood is source of uncertainty

parts.note: grey describes the hair of the old, so it stands for aged
an area is a district or neighbourhood

explanation.surface: An old part of town is a place nobody can be sure about.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation that is unclear and falls between clear categories.
